thread:
jamie: taking over now. brief handoff note said 'primary stepped out; fallback = svc-x-v2 in us-east'. secondary (ravi) not responding to pings. leaving a quick flag here in case something fires during the swap. :wave:

incident-bot: ALERT: latency_slo_violation on /v1/generate (p95 > 1200ms) — incident_id=INC-2026-0314-459. Auto-created by monitoring.

sophia: @jamie thanks for the heads up. I'm looking at the dashboard — saw a sudden spike at 11:03 UTC. client-facing errors still low but user latency is bad.

jamie: can someone confirm which pool is currently serving traffic? handoff doc points to dedicated pool A -> should have autoscaler on.

ravi: (just caught up) sorry was at a meeting. I still have SSH access to the dedicated pool nodes but my phone was on DND. jumping in now.

olivia: pinging the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-spike. key steps: 1) check autoscaler metrics 2) check per-model queue depth 3) fallback routing.

jamie: running quick checks:
```
# list pods with high cpu/mem
kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep svc-x
# check model queue for svc-x
curl -s http://ops-metrics.local/queue?model=svc-x
```

sophia: autoscaler shows 0->2 scaleup attempts failed (timeout). logs indicate a provisioning error with GPU driver.

ravi: that matches what I see on node-34: nvidia-driver stuck during kubelet start. pulling logs, might be an AMI/kernel mismatch after last infra patch.

maya-oncall-lead: escalation checklist: if we can't restore pool in 10m, page infra oncall and follow the 'provision-failure' runbook. page format: @infra-oncall "INC-<id> brief: provisioning failures preventing autoscale in us-east; impact: p95 > 1200ms; attempted remediation: manual node restart; contact: jamie".

kevin-cs: FYI - no customer escalation yet but support has one ticket from large-customer-42 about slow responses. keeping them informed.

jamie: trying manual restart on node-34 now: `sudo systemctl restart kubelet` — will post output.

incident-bot: NOTE: page_threshold for latency_slo_violation is 15m sustained or >20% error rate. Current window is 4m.

ravi: restart failed, kubelet log has `NVIDIA kernel module: missing symbol` repeatedly. this looks like the recent kernel rollout we did last night. we need infra to rollback kernel or reprovision nodes with matching AMI.

maya-oncall-lead: ok, paging infra. @infra-oncall please see INC-2026-0314-459: provisioning/kernel mismatch blocking autoscale; blocker for serving pool A; impact: p95 > 1200ms; primary/secondary handoff in progress (jamie primary).

olivia: temporary mitigation: route a small percentage (5-10%) of traffic to us-west cluster with lower latency. routing config is in edge-proxy -> `route-weight: svc-x: us-west=10`. Doing canary shift now.

jamie: executing canary reroute now, will monitor error budget.

sophia: monitoring shows immediate p95 improvement on canaried requests, overall platform still elevated because only 10% diverted.

kevin-cs: prepping a short customer note: "We've detected elevated latency for generation endpoints in us-east. We're routing traffic to alternate region and working on node reprovisioning. No data loss. We'll update in 30m."

ravi: infra acknowledged the page and said they'll roll back kernel on the affected ASG or reprovision instances. ETA 18-25m.

maya-oncall-lead: summary for handoff: jamie remains primary until pool A is healthy; ravi is acting secondary now that he's back; if kernel rollback fails, escalate to eng-infra manager and product (olivia cc). leave the handoff doc updated with active mitigation steps and links to incident. I'll check back at next status.

jamie: noted. updating handoff doc: `https://redwood.internal/oncall/handoffs/1768349123` with current state + mitigation.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-2026-0314-459 status=mitigating — canary routing applied; infra working on reprovision. next automated check in 10m.

olivia: small operational note for future handoffs: add explicit phone fallback for secondaries and a short 'if primary unavailable' contact list in the top of the handoff message. we've tripped over this twice in the last quarter.

kevin-cs: thanks team. I'll send the customer note once we confirm reprovision completion or 30m timer hits.

ravi: will coordinate with infra oncall and post logs + root cause pointers once nodes are back.

jamie: thanks all — staying on until we have full capacity restored. :v
